response.title: Can a power station recharge my trolling motor batteries overnight at a campsite with no electricity?
response.answer:
Yes, a portable power station can recharge your trolling motor batteries overnight at a campsite without electricity. The key is choosing a power station with enough battery capacity and using the correct charger.

The biggest consideration is that trolling motor batteries store a lot of energy, so smaller portable power stations may only provide a partial recharge.

How it works

Portable power station

Supplies 120V AC electricity from its internal battery.

Your trolling motor battery charger

Plugs into the power station and converts AC power into the correct charging voltage.

Trolling motor batteries

Recharge overnight, provided the power station has enough capacity and the charger is fast enough.

What size power station do you need?

Here are approximate power station capacities for fully recharging different lithium trolling motor battery setups from empty, allowing for charging losses.

Trolling motor battery setup

	

Recommended power station capacity




12V 50Ah lithium

	

800–1,000Wh




12V 100Ah lithium

	

1,500–1,800Wh




24V 100Ah lithium (two 12V batteries)

	

3,000–3,600Wh




36V 100Ah lithium (three 12V batteries)

	

4,500–5,400Wh

These are approximate figures. Lead-acid batteries, partial discharges, and charger efficiency will change the requirements.

For example, if you have two 12V 100Ah lithium batteries powering a 24V trolling motor, a 2,000Wh power station generally won't fully recharge both from empty. But it could provide a substantial partial recharge.

Will it finish charging overnight?

Capacity isn't the only factor. Charger speed matters too.

For a 100Ah battery, approximately:

5A charger: 20+ hours

10A charger: 10–12 hours

20A charger: 5–6 hours

These are estimates from near empty; actual charging times vary by battery chemistry and charger behavior.

Also, check that your power station's AC output can handle the charger's input wattage. Use a charger compatible with your batteries, and keep the equipment dry and properly ventilated.

One other important question: Are you trying to recharge your trolling motor batteries for one night, or for several consecutive nights of camping? That makes a big difference, because a power station also needs a way to recharge itself once its stored energy is depleted.

Here are approximate power station capacities for fully recharging different lithium trolling motor battery setups from empty, allowing for charging losses.

| Trolling motor battery setup | Recommended power station capacity |
|---|---|
| 12V 50Ah lithium | 800–1,000Wh |
| 12V 100Ah lithium | 1,500–1,800Wh |
| 24V 100Ah lithium (two 12V batteries) | 3,000–3,600Wh |
| 36V 100Ah lithium (three 12V batteries) | 4,500–5,400Wh |

These are approximate figures. Lead-acid batteries, partial discharges, and charger efficiency will change the requirements.

For example, if you have two 12V 100Ah lithium batteries powering a 24V trolling motor, a 2,000Wh power station generally won't fully recharge both from empty. But it could provide a substantial partial recharge.

## Will it finish charging overnight?

Capacity isn't the only factor. Charger speed matters too.

For a 100Ah battery, approximately:

- 5A charger: 20+ hours
- 10A charger: 10–12 hours
- 20A charger: 5–6 hours

These are estimates from near empty; actual charging times vary by battery chemistry and charger behavior.

Also, check that your power station's AC output can handle the charger's input wattage. Use a charger compatible with your batteries, and keep the equipment dry and properly ventilated.

{@body const [voltage,setVoltage] = DIL.useState("24")}
{@body const [chem,setChem] = DIL.useState("lithium")}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("100")}
{@body const [discharge,setDischarge] = DIL.useState(80)}
{@body const volts=Number(voltage)}
{@body const ah=Number(capacity)||0}
{@body const required=Math.ceil((volts*ah*discharge/100)/(chem==="lithium"?0.82:0.70)/100)*100}

Recommend an appropriately sized portable power station and estimate overnight charging time.")}>

      <label>Battery type</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={chem} onChange={setChem}>
        <radio value="lithium">Lithium (LiFePO4)</radio>
        <radio value="lead">Lead-acid / AGM</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Battery capacity (Ah at system voltage)</label>
      <radio-group direction="row" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
        <radio value="50">50Ah</radio>
        <radio value="100">100Ah</radio>
        <radio value="125">125Ah</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <row align="center" justify="between">
        <label>Expected battery use each day</label>
        **{discharge}%**
      </row>
      <slider min={20} max={100} step={10} value={discharge} onChange={setDischarge}/>
    </box>
    <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
      <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">ESTIMATED POWER STATION CAPACITY NEEDED</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{required.toLocaleString()} Wh</title>
      <caption>Approximate minimum usable capacity for one recharge, assuming the selected discharge level. Actual results vary.</caption>
    </box>
    <button submit block>Find the right power station <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
